# `js/no-incomplete-accessor-override`

**No overriding only the getter or only the setter of an inherited pair**

| | |
|---|---|
| **Pack** | `@codelaw/rules-js` (npm) · `codelaw-rules-js` (PyPI) |
| **Languages** | JavaScript, JSX, TypeScript, TSX |
| **Turned on by** | `codelaw:js/strict` at `error` |
| **Severity when named without one** | `error` |
| **Options** | none — severity only |
| **Fix** | `manual` — no automatic fix; the steps are under *How to fix* (whether the override needs the other accessor, and what it does, is the author's design) |
| **Stability** | `preview` — runs only with `preview = true` |
| **Since** | 0.5.0 |
| **Ported from** | `eslint-plugin-unicorn/no-incomplete-accessor-override` |

## What it checks

A class that `extends` another class of the same file and defines only `get x` or only `set x`, where the nearest ancestor defining `x` has the other one (or both), is reported at the accessor's key. Defining one accessor replaces the whole inherited property, so the other half is gone. The ancestors are followed through class declarations and `const` aliases; an imported or decorated class, a computed key or a field stops the search.

**Why:** After `set v` alone, reading `v` on the subclass gives `undefined` instead of calling the inherited getter.

## Configuration

Everything below goes in `codelaw.toml` at the repo root. The same keys work as `[tool.codelaw]` in `pyproject.toml` or `"codelaw"` in `package.json` ([SR-CONFIG](../../../records/0110_config.md)).

### Turn it on

**Install the pack** (`codelaw init` does it for the languages it finds):

```bash
npm install --save-dev @codelaw/rules-js
pip install codelaw-rules-js
```

**Then extend a preset that turns it on** — `codelaw:js/strict` sets it to `error`:

```toml
preview = true                        # pack rules are preview today
extends = ["codelaw:js/strict"]
```

- **A rule exists only once its pack is loaded** through `extends`; naming it in `[rules]` without that is an unknown rule id (exit 2).
- **Without `preview = true`** the rule is skipped and codelaw warns that it is preview.

### Severity

```toml
[rules]
"js/no-incomplete-accessor-override" = "warn"    # error | warn | info | off
```

- **`error`** fails the run (exit 1) · **`warn`** fails only with `--max-warnings N` · **`info`** never fails · **`off`** turns it off.
- **Naming it with a severity turns it on** even when no preset does.

### For a group of files

A `[scope.<name>]` gives some files their own setting, applied after `[rules]` — the `tests` scope `codelaw:js/recommended` ships (`**/*.test.*`, `**/*.spec.*`); naming it extends it, so its files stay:

```toml
[scope.tests]
rules = { "js/no-incomplete-accessor-override" = "off" }
```

A scope's `remap` changes whole severities in its files, after everything else: `remap = { error = "warn" }` never fails the run there.

### Warn locally, fail in CI

The `ci` profile runs when `CI` is set; `local` otherwise; `--profile <name>` or `CODELAW_PROFILE` picks one.

```toml
[profile.local.rules]
"js/no-incomplete-accessor-override" = "warn"

[profile.ci.rules]
"js/no-incomplete-accessor-override" = "error"
```

### In `pyproject.toml` or `package.json`

```toml
# pyproject.toml
[tool.codelaw.rules]
"js/no-incomplete-accessor-override" = { severity = "warn" }
```

```json
{
  "codelaw": {
    "rules": {
      "js/no-incomplete-accessor-override": {"severity": "warn"}
    }
  }
}
```

### Silence one finding

An inline `codelaw-ignore` always needs a reason; `expires=`, `warn_days=` and `by=` date it ([SR-LINTER](../../../records/0106_linter.md) decision 6).

- **JavaScript:** `// codelaw-ignore js/no-incomplete-accessor-override: <reason>`
- **Dated:** `// codelaw-ignore js/no-incomplete-accessor-override expires=2026-12-31 by=you@example.com: <reason>`

### Keep today's findings, fail on new ones

```bash
codelaw baseline add --rule js/no-incomplete-accessor-override --expires 2026-12-31 --reason "<why>"
```

See [SR-BASELINE](../../../records/0104_baseline-and-deprecations.md).

### See what applies

```bash
codelaw explain js/no-incomplete-accessor-override       # what it wants, why, how to fix
codelaw check --rule js/no-incomplete-accessor-override  # only this rule
codelaw config --print --for <file>                      # the resolved setting, and where it came from
```

## How to fix

1. Define the missing accessor too; it can forward to the parent: `get v() { return super.v; }`.

## Examples

### JavaScript

#### Don't

```js
class Base {
  get size() {
    return this.n;
  }
  set size(v) {
    this.n = v;
  }
}
class Fixed extends Base {
  set size(v) {}
}
```

#### Do

```js
class Base {
  get size() {
    return this.n;
  }
  set size(v) {
    this.n = v;
  }
}
class Fixed extends Base {
  get size() {
    return super.size;
  }
  set size(v) {}
}
```
